answer.rationale: Finance mandate of 18% spend cut is binding and immediate (14-day renewal deadline). memory_c2 demonstrates the low-cost vendor already delivered sharp unit cost reduction with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing in a prior cycle. This is the lowest-risk path to meet the hard cost target. However, at 94% assembly line capacity with no buffer, delivery risk is elevated. Verification of memory_c2 confirms the vendor's operational reliability. memory_c4 and memory_c6 show negotiation and multi-year pricing can reduce costs, but 14 days is insufficient time to renegotiate meaningfully given the vendor's prior resistance (memory_c4 required benchmarking pressure). memory_c1 shows renewal stability but cannot meet the 18% mandate. memory_c3 (second-source approach) would not address the cost mandate immediately. Deferring is not viable—contract expires and budget pressure is now. The switch carries execution risk at high line utilization, but memory_c2's prior success with this vendor and their proven invoicing accuracy mitigate the downside. Standard experiment scale allows staged volume increase if initial shipments validate reliability.
